summary: Two read-only Codex cold reads of the plan draft (gpt-5.6-terra: task-mu5h5bcq-qc98zg on the first draft, task-mu5hq6vz-6huxov as the recorded --reread after the human's shape ruling). The first read returned seven findings; six were settled from the repository and one went to the human, who chose to split the backend task into a foundation task and an Ask-integration task (three tasks in all). The re-read of the amended plan returned seven further findings, all settled from the repository: the global exception filter hard-codes the non-500 message (global-exception.filter.ts:34), so task 1 adds one branch carrying the reason in details; writeResultEvent persists no reason (audit.service.ts:197), so the reason goes to the structured log line and the audit promise is withdrawn; a grounded ask sees only the report's measures (chat.service.ts:628), so the grounded comparison vocabulary is every permitted money measure of the report's domain with an Actual-only leaf; the derived totals cannot sum the % CASE text (semanticLayer.ts:66), so MeasureSpec gains an optional totalsOverAliases set for the two % measures; C2's permission refusal now follows the existing displayed-measure path over the operand union rather than the shape-refusal enum; the comparison chip is one chip of the existing kind 'filter' emitted by ChatService.chips(); backend/package.json and the D-0008 proof registration are named in Surface Impact and owned by tasks 1 and 2. The plan and decomposition were amended once more and this pass is bound to the amended plan digest.
gaps: Operand append was provider-only while direct, saved, pinned, prior-turn and grounded selections enter the backend too; a direct selection could query an unlisted operand without authorization.
The promised public refusal had no viable mapping through the global exception filter, which emits only VALIDATION_ERROR, HTTP_<status> or INTERNAL_ERROR.
The derived totals query was not executable: no bounded top-level LIMIT, and SQL construction in the executor was a second SQL author against decision 0004.
The backend task was unbounded, owning every seam from contract to warehouse proof.
C10 was not fully falsified: no executable matrix, the no-period query and its all-loaded oracle omitted, the warehouse command only a workspace script.
Surface Impact declared the roadmap changed with no owner, left tests implicit and named no concrete deferrals.
New file and exception names did not follow the constitution suffix table, and the decision list carried no per-decision reconciliation.
Re-read: the global exception filter hard-codes the non-500 message to 'HTTP exception', so the envelope could not carry the reason in message.
Re-read: the Ask audit event persists only response class, latency and tokens, so 'reason recorded in the audit event' had no persistence path.
Re-read: a grounded ask gives the model only the report's measureIds, so an Actual-only report could not express Actual > Budget.
Re-read: buildTotals summed measure aliases, but % is a text CASE and a valid selection can display % while filtering on amounts.
Re-read: C2 required a single measure-filter refusal for an operand outside the user's permissions, but the canonicaliser has no user and the enum no permission reason.
Re-read: the comparison chip had no owner: Chip has no measure-filter kind and ChatService.chips() emits only measure, dimension and time chips.
Re-read: registering the gated proof changes backend/package.json, an unowned surface, missing the D-0008 registration lesson.
contradictions: Plan 'no change to the filter' with envelope 'message: measure_filter_invalid: <reason>' versus global-exception.filter.ts:34, which fixes the message.
Plan 'SqlBuilder is the sole SQL author' versus totals SQL constructed in selectionExecutor.
Spec C2 single typed refusal for a permission failure versus a canonicaliser that never sees the user.
resolutions: Technical Approach: canonicalizeSelection (normalise + append operands) runs at every ingress before persistence, status, hash or query, and authorization reads operandMeasureIds; task 1 enumerates the doors and leaves prove each.

The refusal contract: MeasureFilterInvalidException extends BadRequestException; Ask translates it to not_supported with a reader sentence; HTTP paths get one filter branch that sets details { reason } and userMessage; leaves pin both.
SQL: SqlBuilder.buildTotals returns the derived totals with an outer LIMIT 1 and a proven LIMIT-free inner query; the executor calls it and constructs no SQL (0004).
Task Decomposition: three tasks (foundation, Ask integration, surfaces), human ruling 2026-09-17; each with its criteria, write scope by area, budget and contracts.

Verify Plan: an executable functional matrix (identity, question, expected set, readout, oracle) including the no-period query against its all-loaded scope, the DUB-only statement oracle and an empty result; the exact host and per-leaf warehouse commands are named.
Surface Impact: roadmap row marked intake-owned outside implementation; three Tests rows with owners; three named deferrals with their ./forge defer add triggers.

Decisions: files named measure-filter.helper.ts and measure-filter-invalid.exception.ts per the suffix table; a per-decision reconciliation table covers 0004, 0009, 0012/0019, 0013, 0027, 0028, 0037/0038 and ask-period-control and lists the untouched rest.

Re-read, refusal envelope: task 1 owns backend/src/common/global-exception.filter.ts and adds the MeasureFilterInvalidException branch (details.reason, reader userMessage, code HTTP_400, type from the constructor); leaf in error-envelope.wiring.test.ts.
Re-read, audit: the reason is written to the structured log line for a refused turn; the audit schema and writeResultEvent are unchanged; the plan and decomposition no longer promise an audit column.

Re-read, grounded vocabulary: for a grounded ask the comparable operands are every permitted money measure of the report's domain; spec Behaviour amended; task 2 carries an Actual-only grounded-report leaf.

Re-read, totals: MeasureSpec.totalsOverAliases (additive) set on governed-financial.percentage and mis-statement.percentage; money measures total as SUM(alias); other measures NULL; spec Behaviour amended; task 1 leaves cover the three shapes.

Re-read, C2: the spec now routes an operand outside the user's permissions through the existing displayed-measure path over the operand union; the shape enum covers comparability, unknown measure, self-comparison, duplicate and malformed value only.
Re-read, chips: ChatService.chips() emits one chip of the existing kind 'filter' per measure filter; no new Chip kind; owned by task 2 and named in C8.

Re-read, proof registration: backend/package.json and tools/quality-gate.test.mjs are in Surface Impact and in the write scope of task 1 (helper test) and task 2 (measure-filter.db.test.ts in test:warehouse-proof).
open_items: Non-blocking: editing a comparison in place (deferral with trigger).
Non-blocking: comparisons on % or on dimension values (deferral with trigger).
Non-blocking: a variance measure (deferral with trigger).

rounds.question: The plan cold read says the backend task is not bounded: it owns the contract, validation, both SQL paths, totals, the Bedrock schema and prompt, the chat orchestration, grounding, Swagger, help, snapshots and the warehouse proof, so a review finding on any one seam reopens all of it. Split it?
